title: SLO metric contract templates and dashboard culling guide
content:
Purpose
------
This is a working checklist + template set for onboarding services into Redwood’s SLO-driven observability stack, and a pragmatic guide for pruning / prioritizing dashboards. Aim: reduce dashboard sprawl, ensure metric contracts are well defined, and make tracing anchors predictable for fast RCA.

Audience
--------
Primary: service owners and engineers preparing a service for SLOs and production runbooks. Secondary: oncall, SREs, and product owners who need clear instrumentation expectations.

Quick summary (TL;DR)
---------------------
- Give every new customer-visible surface 3 core SLIs (availability/error-rate, p50/p95 latency, user-impactful correctness indicator).
- Use the metric contract template below for each SLI. Store contract as YAML in repo alongside README.
- Maintain a single team-owned dashboard per service (exceptions for very large services). Trim panels by cost-and-actionability.
- Tracing: standardize span names + an anchor span per request path to enable session reconstruction.
- Sampling/cost: prefer severity-weighted trace sampling; set a query budget for dashboards that use trace joins.

Onboarding checklist (service owner)
-----------------------------------
1) Define customer-facing endpoints and user journeys (list top 3).
2) For each journey, pick 1 availability SLI, 1 latency SLI, 1 quality SLI. Document rationale.
3) Fill metric contract template for each SLI and commit to telemetry repo.
4) Implement metrics with the agreed labels/dimensions and unit semantics.
5) Add one minimal dashboard with: summary row (SLO burn, error %, latency quantiles), a hot-path traces panel, and error sample list.
6) Add runbook stub linking SLO -> pager policy -> first responder.
7) Request SRE review: instrument sampling, dashboards cost estimate, and checklist sign-off.

Metric contract template (copy into telemetry repo)
---------------------------------------------------
- name: "service_namespace.sli_name"
- owner: "team-name / oncall rota"
- description: "short description of what the SLI measures and why it matters to customers"
- intent: "availability | latency | correctness | throughput"
- unit: "milliseconds | percent | count"
- numerator: "promql | sql | metric expression"
- denominator: "promql | sql | metric expression (if applicable)"
- labels: ["tenant_id", "route", "model_variant"]
- aggregation_window: "60s | 5m | 1h"
- evaluation_frequency: "60s | 5m"
- alert_thresholds: {"warning": "<value>", "critical": "<value>"}
- accepted_error_modes: "list of known error cases and mitigation steps"
- data_retention_for_sli: "90d | 365d"
- linked_playbook: "confluence or runbook url"

Notes on numerator/denominator canonicalization
------------------------------------------------
- Prefer event-level counters with clear success/failure semantics. Example: http_request_total{status_code=~"5.."} / http_request_total.
- Avoid derived success heuristics that rely on ML output unless accompanied by stable testset evaluation traces.
- Unit semantics must be enforced at ingestion (no mixing ms and s).

Dashboard culling & prioritization heuristics
---------------------------------------------
Goal: one well-maintained dashboard per service that answers the 3 SLI questions + one operational view per mixed-traffic model route. Use the following rules when reviewing dashboards:
- Keep if it is part of SLO alerting or used in oncall runbook.
- Keep if it helps a postmortem or is explicitly referenced in a runbook.
- Consider merging panels if they share identical query shapes and label slices.
- Remove if age > 9 months and not viewed or saved by a stakeholder.
- Cap of 25 panels per service dashboard; if exceeded, split into "summary" + "deep-dive" (deep-dive must be team-owned and audited).
- Tag dashboards with owner, last-review date, cost estimate (query credits), and human-readable intent.

Pruning process (quarterly review)
----------------------------------
1) Snapshot dashboard inventory and compute query-cost per panel for last 30 days.
2) Notify owners of dashboards in the audit window.
3) For each dashboard: keep/merge/prioritize/archive based on heuristics above.
4) Archive dashboards to the archival folder and surface a short diff to the retained dashboard.
5) Reassign ownership if owner unreachable.

Tracing anchors and span naming conventions
-----------------------------------------
- Every request entering Redwood surface should create a root span: redwood.root.request with attributes: service, route, customer_id (when available), model_variant.
- Hot-path spans should use stable names: compute.kv_cache, model.decode, router.fanout, kv.cache_lookup. Avoid ad-hoc names like "step1".
- Annotate spans with token counts and batch ids for inference requests to make token-attribution easier. Use tags: token_count:int, batch_id:string.
- Include an "analysis.anchor" span that marks the logical user-turn boundaries (useful for multi-turn traces).

Sampling strategy guidance
-------------------------
- Default: severity-weighted reservoir sampling where traces with errors have sampling_factor = 10x baseline.
- For high-volume inference endpoints, use adaptive sampling: keep all traces with latency > p95 and sample ~0.1% of p50 traces.
- Maintain a query budget per dashboard (e.g., 200 trace-queries/month) and surface it in the dashboard meta.

Cost/benefit rules for panels
-----------------------------
- If a panel requires trace joins that cost > 0.5 query credit / view, consider replacing with pre-aggregated metric.
- Use small-sample trace widgets sparingly on public dashboards; put them into deep-dive dashboards instead.

Example SLI mapping (toy service: inference-gateway)
-----------------------------------------------------
- SLI-1 availability: numerator = sum(http_request_total{code!~"5.."}), denominator = sum(http_request_total), window = 5m.
- SLI-2 latency: p95(http_request_duration_ms{route="/v1/generate"}) over 5m.
- SLI-3 correctness proxy: fraction of requests that pass golden-prompt check within model run.

Open questions / tradeoffs for discussion
---------------------------------------
- How do we encode ML-quality SLIs without coupling to ephemeral gold datasets? (suggested: store a stable evaluation-set run daily and surface drift alerts).
- Do we force a strict 25-panel cap? Some platform services need more; maybe make exceptions after cost review.
- Agree on enforcement: metric-contract validation in CI vs periodic manual audits.

Action items (next 2 weeks)
--------------------------
- Maya: draft CI schema for metric contract validation (YAML linter) — due 2025-03-10.
- Ethan: build dashboard-cost script to compute credits per panel — due 2025-03-05.
- Sofia: propose sampling presets for inference-heavy routes and add to telemetry repo — due 2025-03-12.
- Owners: tag dashboards with review date and owner by 2025-03-07.

Notes to reviewers
------------------
This is intentionally prescriptive to force choices. Expect iterations. Add examples to the telemetry repo so teams can copy/paste the contract and dashboard templates.

- Draft runbook template: CONFLUENCE-OBS-1024

--------------------------------------
